task.description: WF-02 Step 2c -- hard security gate on ELIXIR-DEV's Step 2a implementation of Letflow.Api.Context (REQ-072), the single tenant-scoping mechanism every future S4 route calls to derive its Ecto :prefix. Assess all of INV-1..INV-8 against the actual diff (git diff main...HEAD) and record PASS/FAIL per applicable invariant.

result.summary:
Scope test: this diff adds a new tenant-scoping primitive on the request path (lib/letflow/api/context.ex's scoped_repo_opts/1, the mechanism every future lookup-by-ID handler will call to derive :prefix) -- squarely a tenant-data path per SECURITY-REVIEWER's scope test. Full review, not a surface read.

INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. Read scoped_repo_opts/1 line by line (lib/letflow/api/context.ex:213-224) and its private helper tenant_id_from_auth_context/1 (:226-231). Confirmed: (a) it is genuinely 1-arity -- function_exported?(Context, :scoped_repo_opts, 2/3/4) all refute in the test file, and the source has no additional clause or default arg; (b) the function body reads exactly one field, conn.assigns[:auth_context][:tenant_id], via a single pattern match `%{tenant_id: tenant_id} when not is_nil(tenant_id) -> {:ok, tenant_id}`; grepped the whole file myself for conn.params, conn.query_params, conn.req_headers, get_req_header -- the only get_req_header call in the file is in incoming_trace_id/1 (trace-id handling, unrelated function, no tenant dimension); (c) both error branches (:missing_auth_context from the :error clause, :invalid_tenant_id from TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1's error passthrough) return a bare {:error, _} tuple -- traced every path, there is no third clause and no fallback that could produce {:ok, prefix: _} without going through TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant(tenant_id) using the auth_context-derived tenant_id. No nil-check ordering bug, no ||/Map.get/3 default: the `when not is_nil(tenant_id)` guard means a nil tenant_id in auth_context falls to :missing_auth_context, not a silently-nil prefix. tenant_id is never accepted as a caller-supplied argument -- confirmed by signature inspection, matching AC6.

INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability) -- APPLIES, PASS. Read test/letflow/api/context_test.exs's cross-tenant-404 describe block (lines 160-244) in full. This is a real demonstration, not mocked: two tenants provisioned via TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 (real schema creation), a probe table replayed into both real schemas via TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/2 with a genuine Ecto.Migration (test/support/req072_probe.ex), a row genuinely inserted only into tenant B's schema via Repo.insert!(prefix: tenant_b.schema_name). The byte-identity test calls Repo.get(Probe, tenant_b_row_id, prefix: schema_a) (cross-tenant, real cross-schema query that finds nothing because tenant A's schema genuinely has no such row) versus Repo.get(Probe, Ecto.UUID.generate(), prefix: schema_a) (never-existed), both routed through the same not_found_response/4 helper which raises if a row is unexpectedly found (guards against a test-setup defect masking a real leak), then asserts resp_1.status == resp_2.status and resp_1.resp_body == resp_2.resp_body -- a real byte-for-byte comparison, not vacuous (conn_a pins :trace_id to a fixed value in setup specifically so that field cannot introduce spurious variance, isolating the comparison to the property under test). The query-count test attaches real telemetry ([:letflow, :repo, :query]) around two genuine Repo.get/3 calls and compares counts -- not simulated, an actual counter incremented by real query telemetry events, reset between the two calls. Neither test short-circuits early: both reach and execute the interesting assertion.

INV-6 (no raw SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. schema_name_for_tenant/1's result flows into {:ok, prefix: schema_name}, spread as a plain :prefix keyword option into Repo.get/Repo.insert! calls -- Ecto's own SQL adapter handles prefix quoting/validation internally; no string concatenation or interpolation of schema_name into any raw query anywhere in the new code (grep for Repo.query across the changed files: zero hits).

INV-4 (secrets by reference) -- NOT APPLICABLE, no secret material resolved, logged, or serialised in this diff. Verified via grep (System.get_env and hardcoded-secret heuristic patterns): zero hits in the changed files.

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. grep -rn "Repo.query" against context.ex and api_pipeline.ex: zero hits.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes) -- APPLIES, PASS. grep for the bare `{:ok, _} = ` pattern in context.ex: zero hits. Both scoped_repo_opts/1's internal calls (tenant_id_from_auth_context/1, TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1) are handled via full case/with-style tagged-tuple matching, no bare pattern match that could raise on realistic tenant-controlled input.

INV-2, INV-3 -- NOT APPLICABLE (S4 response-shaping / S5 sandboxing preconditions not yet reached by this diff; no API response type or scripting runtime touched).

Trace-id mechanism: assign_trace_id/1 (context.ex:156-164) sets the caller-supplied (or generated) trace id onto conn.assigns, a plain response header via put_resp_header/3, and Logger.metadata(trace_id: trace_id). None of these are injection-sensitive sinks: a response header value is not a format string or file path, and Logger.metadata/1 stores the value as structured metadata (a term in a keyword list), not interpolated into a log format string in a way that could be exploited -- Elixir's :logger backend does not re-parse metadata values as format directives. Truncation to 256 bytes bounds the value; the module's own doc correctly notes no shape validation is performed, matching R-Co's port, and this is genuinely safe given the two actual sinks (header, log metadata), not merely assumed safe by precedent -- I traced both call sites myself rather than trusting the design doc's claim.

Moduledoc honesty check (grep-tension workaround): read the entire file. Confirmed zero real uses of Process.put/2, Process.get/1, or :ets anywhere in context.ex -- grep -n "Process.put|Process.get|:ets\." lib/letflow/api/context.ex returns zero hits. The moduledoc's wording avoiding the literal grep substrings while still stating the invariant in prose is honest, not obscuring a real violation.

Scope (git diff main...HEAD --stat): only lib/letflow/api/context.ex (new), lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex (plug-mount edit), test/support/req072_probe.ex (new fixture), test/letflow/api/context_test.exs (new), the design doc, and this run's own bookkeeping (requirements.yaml, status files, handoffs/, registry.json) changed. Confirmed via targeted diff: lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex and lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex show 0 diff lines -- neither was touched.

All applicable invariants verified PASS with no fallback path found. This module correctly and structurally discharges INV-1/INV-5 once for every future route that composes its output, per the design's own reasoning.
